findings.description: Target is t.substr(slash)+path.substr(min(path.size(), loc.path.size()))+query. The clamp empties the remainder on an exact match, so GET /api?cmd=whoami emits GET /exec?cmd=whoami HTTP/1.1, three tokens, and a strict parser runs whoami; bare GET /api runs id. No encoding. Requires a URI naming the route with no trailing space, an exact location match and a strict reader.
findings.title: The min()-clamped slice leaves the URI intact on an exact match, so an attacker query alone executes a chosen command in a 3-token line, with no encoding

limitations: Needs a strict 3-token reader and exact match
methods: Strict peer, verbatim line, token count, exact 3-token exec
